prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for everyone — the right one depends on your zip code, health needs, budget, whether you want in‑person help, and whether you need help with ACA subsidies, HSAs, QSEHRA/SEP, etc. That said, here’s a practical way to find a great broker in Kansas City who understands self‑employed needs, plus some concrete options you can use right away.

How to pick a broker who’s good for someone self‑employed
- Prefer an independent agent/broker who can compare multiple carriers (not captive to one insurer).  
- Look for experience with individual & ACA plans, marketplace enrollments and subsidy calculations.  
- Make sure they’re licensed in Missouri — ask for license number and check with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance.  
- Ask about fees: many brokers are paid by carriers for individual plans (no direct fee), but confirm.  
- Ask specific questions: experience with self‑employed clients, knowledge of QSEHRA/SEP/HSAs, how they’ll compare networks, out‑of‑pocket vs premium tradeoffs, how they handle claims issues.  
- Check reviews: Google/Yelp/BBB and NAHU membership are useful signals.

Places and services to find a broker right now
- NAHU’s “Find an Agent” directory — locate certified agents in Kansas City.  
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — verify licenses and see complaints.  
- HealthCare.gov or HealthSherpa — good for comparing ACA plans and finding certified application counselors (assisters) and agents who can enroll you and check subsidy eligibility.  
- Online broker platforms (useful if you prefer mostly remote/electronic help): eHealth, GoHealth, HealthSherpa. They compare multiple carriers and can be quicker for quotes.  
- Major local carrier agents: Blue KC (Blue Cross Blue Shield of Kansas City) and UnitedHealthcare have local agent networks if you prefer dealing with a known carrier — useful if you have a strong preference for a specific insurer.

Questions to ask any candidate broker
- “How many individual/self‑employed clients do you work with?”  
- “Do you represent multiple carriers or are you captive to one?”  
- “How do you get paid?”  
- “Can you show me plan comparisons with total yearly cost (premiums + expected OOP) for my providers?”  
- “Will you help with subsidy/Marketplace enrollment and with claims problems later?”

If you want, I can:
- Look up 3–5 top-rated independent brokers/agencies near your Kansas City zip code, with phone numbers and review snippets; or  
- Walk you through the exact plan comparison (if you give age, household size, income, preferred doctors/hospitals, and zip code).

Which would you prefer?
